title.suggested: Allen's letter on the death of Andy Bowen

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch printed a letter from Tom Allen blaming Andy Bowen's seconds for not stopping his fatal fight with George Lavigne and predicting that boxing would survive any ban.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Sunday Morning, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, December 23, 1894, page 10.

facts.fact: Allen wrote to the Post-Dispatch blaming Andy Bowen's seconds for his death after the fight with George Lavigne
facts.quote: Had Bowen been fortunate enough to have a man behind him who understood his business, I believe he would be still in the land of the living.

facts.fact: Allen said he believed in fighting in the open air and that boxing would outlast the New Orleans clubs
facts.quote: I am a firm believer in fighting in the open air, and if Bowen's death puts a quietus on legalized glove contests, the old-time methods will come into vogue once more.

notes: Matches the facts-index line marked 000 ('Allen writes a letter about the Bowen/Lavigne fight'), which has no unique id. Signed 'Thomas Allen, Retired Champion of the World.'
